solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A work by Woolf she thought Eliot might review

indicators.note: to review something is to go over it again, here reworking the letters into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A reader guesses that T. S. Eliot might have written a review of one of Virginia Woolf's books.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliot and Woolf were contemporaries in literary London, which makes the review plausible; the fifteen letters of the three words rearrange into the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf's 1927 novel, set on the Isle of Skye, bears this title.

clue.text: I concede my title, dad — sorry

indicators.note: sorry in the sense of in a poor or wretched state, so the letters are in a mess

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone apologises to their father while grudgingly conceding a point about a title.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb is used to grant a point before going on, the same job as the phrase of concession.

clue.text: Plump, but not because of fish

indicators.note: but not tells us to leave the following words' letters out of what came before

parts.note: chubby means plump
by can mean because of, as in 'shocked by the news'

explanation.surface: Someone insists a person is plump for reasons that have nothing to do with eating fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish of the carp family, common in European rivers.

clue.text: Endure personnel cuts across the board

indicators.note: cuts here means slices into, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: to tough it out is to endure hardship to the end
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: Staff must put up with job cuts imposed in every department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Personnel cuts' reads as redundancies, but the personnel department is the piece doing the cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Across the board means affecting everything, in every part, exactly as the adverb does.

clue.text: Make a boob warmer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to bungle or fumble, a boob being a blunder
second meaning: a tube of fur or fabric for keeping the hands warm

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an item of underwear; boob is the British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for botching something, such as a catch, and a noun for a cylindrical hand-warming accessory.

clue.text: Spoiler alert means youth will interrupt definitive new auction

parts.note: the definite article, THE, is the definitive word

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle, so these pieces go inside the others

parts.note: a resale is selling again, a new sale
a way is a means of doing something
a son is a young male

explanation.surface: A warning that a young bidder is about to disrupt a final, decisive sale.
explanation.walkthrough: THE is the definite article, which the clue calls definitive.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase is said wearily about the one person who always ruins things, a warning of a spoilsport.

clue.text: In primarily heated talks, time's run out — but remember your point

indicators.note: In tells us what follows sits inside the letters given by the first words
primarily means taking the first letter of each of the words heated and talks

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

indicators.note: run here is to run through, to pierce, so the time piece goes inside

parts.note: out as in out of date, old hat
T is the abbreviation for time
though can mean but, as in 'it's good, though dear'

explanation.surface: During heated negotiations the time is up, so speakers are told to keep their point for later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time's run out' is a single phrase on the surface, but it splits: time, a run-through indicator, and out meaning old hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase asks someone to keep an idea in mind for later, so remember is a direct paraphrase.

clue.text: You shouldn't have crackling like old film

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, which 'you shouldn't have' expresses

indicators.note: crackling suggests something breaking up, so the letters of like are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is thanked politely for a gift of pork crackling, like an old film scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Crackling looks like a noun, the crispy pork skin, but works as the anagram signal. Ta is British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A talkie was an early film with a soundtrack, the name dating from the end of the silent era.

clue.text: Asian Cup match supplied with commentary

indicators.note: commentary is spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: in British football a cup tie is a knockout match

explanation.surface: An Asian Cup football match is broadcast with commentary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian Cup' reads as one tournament, but the definition is just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Thailand, in south-east Asia, is a native of an Asian nation.

clue.text: Sick from dips in cold menu

indicators.note: to dip in is to go into, so these letters go inside the next piece

parts.note: bare as in exposed and unheated, a cold bare room
ill means sick
off can mean from, as in 'get off the bus'

explanation.surface: Someone feels ill after eating cold dips from a menu.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill of fare is an old-fashioned term for a list of dishes offered at a restaurant.

clue.text: Unacceptable way to discharge advice from the horse's mouth?

definitions.text: Unacceptable way to discharge advice from the horse's mouth?

parts.note: the surface reading: an improper way of getting rid of something, the literal sense of illegal dumping
the setter's reading: a racing tip passed on the fly, as if straight from the horse

explanation.surface: Racing tips straight from a horse would be an improper way to pass on advice.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly-tipping is the British term for dumping waste illegally; the second reading plays on a tip from the horse's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal dumping of rubbish on land not licensed for it is an antisocial way of getting rid of waste.

clue.text: Day's work in a restaurant suited?

definitions.text: Day's work in a restaurant suited?

parts.note: business done over a meal at midday
the diners wear business suits, not that the place is suitable

explanation.surface: Is a restaurant a suitable place to do a day's work?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suited' looks like 'suitable' but describes the suit-wearing executives at the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A working midday meal for influential executives, where deals are discussed over food.

clue.text: Quickly fixed snack will break it!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: at speed, as an adverb
third meaning: a period without food, which eating breaks, as in breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one word; the last hints at breakfast, the meal that breaks a fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means rapidly, firmly secured, and a spell of abstaining from food.

clue.text: So a mass public brawl yet no-one pays?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a disorderly fight that everyone joins
second meaning: something given without charge to everybody

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally the phrase also says everything is free, hence the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is used for an uncontrolled melee and, literally, for something available at no cost to anyone.

clue.text: Warehouse graduation party, so it appears?

indicators.note: the picture is of a party dressed up in a gown, so one piece is wrapped in the other

parts.note: a gown is worn at a graduation ceremony
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A graduation party is held in a warehouse, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: A godown is a warehouse in India and East Asia, from Malay.
explanation.definitionFit: In South and East Asian trade a godown is a storage building at a port, a word borrowed into English.

clue.text: Christmas past, spring yet to appear

parts.note: something yet to appear is not there, so no spring
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Christmas is over and the spring season has still not arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Past' signals an old spelling; spring is the water source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaic spelling of Noel, the Christmas carol word, as in The First Nowell.

clue.text: Chief objective hiding in it?

indicators.note: one piece is tucked away inside the other

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman chief or commander
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A meeting's main aim is concealed within its list of business.
explanation.walkthrough: Aga, a Turkish commander, is a crossword favourite; the whole clue also says a good list of items holds the main aim, and hints at a hidden one.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items to be discussed at a meeting should include its chief objective.

clue.text: Last man to get away from the state borders

indicators.note: the word state borders what is left, sitting either side of it

parts.note: to say is to state

indicators.note: the man piece leaves the word the, taken out of it

parts.note: taken as written
he stands for a man

explanation.surface: The last man standing wants to escape over the state's borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last man' reads as one phrase, but last is the verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to remain or endure, and to stay means to remain in place.

clue.text: With fog bad on river, always given priority

indicators.note: bad as in spoilt, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
ay, or aye, is an old poetic word for always

explanation.surface: Fog on a river is so bad that shipping is always given precedence.
explanation.walkthrough: Ay for ever is poetic, as in 'for aye'.
explanation.definitionFit: Right of way is the precedence one road user or vessel has over another.

clue.text: Bar manager keeps a cuckoo

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the bar piece contains the next letter

parts.note: a rod is a bar
taken as written
someone who runs a business is its runner

explanation.surface: The pub manager keeps a mad person on the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: Cuckoo looks like an adjective for crazy, but it names the bird family.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadrunner of the American south-west is a ground-dwelling bird of the cuckoo family.

clue.text: Family of authors kept up with Latin

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: had is the past tense of have, to keep

explanation.surface: A literary family kept going with their Latin studies.
explanation.walkthrough: Roald Dahl and his granddaughter Sophie are both authors.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl, his wife's novels aside, plus granddaughter Sophie Dahl form a writing dynasty.

clue.text: Position behind tower

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the back part, the place at the back

explanation.walkthrough: Tower reads as a noun, but here it is a verb meaning rise up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for the back position and a verb for rising to a great height.

clue.text: Rankings announced: English golfer went up

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, so we want a word that is heard the same

parts.note: rows are ranks or lines

explanation.surface: Golf rankings are announced and an English player has climbed them.
explanation.walkthrough: Justin Rose is an English golfer and former US Open champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Justin Rose is an English major-winning golfer, and the word is also the past tense of rise.

clue.text: IQ = 2 x 8?

parts.note: the intelligence score is being stated
two by eight is a size of sawn timber, as well as a sum giving sixteen

explanation.surface: An equation sets someone's IQ at two times eight, a dismal score.
explanation.walkthrough: Timber is sold by section, so a two-by-eight is a plank; 2 x 8 = 16 is a very low IQ.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile means extremely stupid, comparing a dim person to a piece of wood.
